source.title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing

accepted.question_text: Does every regular tournament, meaning an orientation of a complete graph in which each vertex has the same in-degree and out-degree, have its arc set decomposable into Hamilton cycles?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 (Kelly 196?). The arc set of every regular tournament can be decomposed into Hamilton cycles.

accepted.question_text: Does every k-arc-strong tournament T=(V,A) admit a decomposition of its arc set into k pairwise disjoint sets A1,...,Ak such that each spanning subdigraph Di=(V,Ai) is strongly connected?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.3 (Bang-Jensen and Yeo, 2004). The arc set of every k-arc-strong tournament T = (V, A) can be decomposed into k disjoint sets A1, . . . , Ak such that each of the spanning subdigraphs Di = (V, Ai), i = 1, 2, . . . , k is strongly connected.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a natural number K such that every K-arc-strong digraph D=(V,A) can be decomposed into two arc-disjoint strong spanning subdigraphs D1=(V,A1) and D2=(V,A2)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.5 (Bang-Jensen and Yeo, 2004). There exists a natural number K such that every K-arc-strong digraph D = (V, A) can be decomposed into two arc-disjoint strong spanning subdigraphs D1 = (V, A1) and D2 = (V, A2).

accepted.question_text: Does every 3-strong tournament contain two arc-disjoint Hamilton cycles?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.8 (Thomassen, 1982). Every 3-strong tournament has 2-arc-disjoint Hamilton cycles.

accepted.question_text: Given a tournament whose vertex set can be partitioned into t disjoint subsets inducing k-strong subtournaments, can one additionally prescribe vertices x1,...,xt in advance and require xi to belong to Vi for each i?
accepted.context_brief: Prescribed vertices in strong tournament decompositions

evidence.quote: Question 2.10. Can we also specify t vertices x1, x2, . . . , xt and find V1, . . . , Vt as above such that xi ∈ Vi holds for i = 1, 2, . . . , t?

accepted.question_text: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether the underlying undirected graph UG(D) of a digraph D contains a 2-factor C1,C2,...,Ck such that C1 is a directed cycle in D, while the other cycles Ci for i>1 need not respect the orientations of arcs in D?

evidence.quote: Question 2.13. Is there a polynomial algorithm for deciding whether the underlying graph UG(D) of a digraph D contains a 2-factor C1, C2, . . . , Ck such that C1 is a directed cycle in D, while Ci, i > 1 does not have to respect the orientations of arcs in D?

accepted.question_text: What is the computational complexity of deciding, for a 2-edge-coloured bipartite graph B=(U,V,E), whether B contains two edge-disjoint perfect matchings M1 and M2 such that every edge of M1 has colour 1 while M2 may use edges of either colour?
accepted.context_brief: Colored perfect matchings in bipartite graphs

evidence.quote: Question 2.14. What is the complexity of the following problem: given a 2-edge-coloured bipartite graph B = (U, V, E); decide whether B has two edge-disjoint perfect matchings M1, M2 so that every edge of M1 has colour 1, while M2 may use edges of both colours?

accepted.question_text: For each maximum degree d, determine or estimate the smallest f(d) such that any finite graph G of maximum degree at most d with at most d pendant edges pre-coloured, and with no two incident pre-coloured edges sharing a colour, can have that pre-colouring extended to a proper edge-colouring of G using d+f(d) colours.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. Estimate the minimum f = f(d) such that the following holds. Let G be a (finite) graph of maximum degree at most d with at most d pendant edges pre-coloured (with no two incident pre-coloured edges having the same colour). Then this pre-colouring can be extended to a proper (d + f)-edge-colouring of G.

accepted.question_text: Let d tend to infinity. Is there a function g(d)=o(d/log d) such that every graphing G of maximum degree at most d admits a measurable partition of its vertex space I=[0,1] into A∪B for which every vertex x has nearly balanced degrees into A and B, meaning the two degrees differ by at most g(d)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Let d → ∞. Prove that there is g(d) = o(d/ log d) such that any graphing G of maximum degree at most d admits a measurable partition I = A ∪ B such that for every vertex x is (A, B)-balanced, meaning that its degrees into A and into B differ by at most g(d).

accepted.question_text: If C is a universal constant such that every planar n-vertex graph G satisfies the diagonal Ramsey bound R(G,G)≤Cn, can one always take C≤12?

evidence.quote: Question 4.1. Is C ≤ 12?

accepted.question_text: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs an equitable k-colouring of any graph G whose maximum Ore degree θ(G)=max{d(x)+d(y):xy∈E(G)} satisfies θ(G)<2k?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithms for equitable colouring under Ore bounds

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Is there a polynomial algorithm for constructing an equitable k-coloring of any graph G with θ(G) < 2k?

accepted.question_text: Suppose T1,T2,T3 are edge-disjoint spanning trees in a graph G on n vertices. Must there exist a cyclic ordering of the edges in E(T1)∪E(T2)∪E(T3) such that every n−1 cyclically consecutive edges form a spanning tree?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3. Let T1, T2, T3 be edge-disjoint spanning trees in a graph G on n vertices (so each tree has n − 1 edges). Then there exists a cyclic ordering of the edges in E(T1) ∪ E(T2) ∪ E(T3) such that every n − 1 cyclically consecutive edges in that ordering form a spanning tree.

accepted.question_text: If B={b1,...,br} and B'={b'1,...,b'r} are disjoint bases of a matroid, do there exist permutations of B and B' whose concatenation forms a cyclic ordering in which every r cyclically consecutive elements form a base?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. Let B = {b1, . . . , br} and B0 = {b0 1 , . . . , b0 r} be two disjoint bases of a matroid. Then there is a permutation (bπ(1), . . . , bπ(r)) of the elements of B and a permutation (b0 π0(1), . . . , b0 π0(r)) of the elements of B0 such that the combined sequence (bπ(1), . . . , bπ(r), b0 π0(1), . . . , b0 π0(r)) is a cyclic ordering in which every r cyclically consecutive elements form a base.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a function f:N→R+ such that every hypergraph H satisfies χs(H)≤f(χd(H))·r(H), where r(H) is the maximum edge size, χs(H) is the strong chromatic number, and χd(H) is the maximum chromatic number among derived graphs obtained by choosing one pair from each hyperedge?

evidence.quote: Question 4.5. Does there exist a function f : N → R+ so that for every hypergraph H we have χs(H) ≤ f(χd(H)) · r(H) ?

accepted.question_text: For a graph G on [n], let Q(G) be the family of independent vertex subsets and let s(G) be the size of a largest antichain in Q(G). Under what conditions on G do we have s(G) equal, or asymptotically close, to the size of the largest layer max_r |Q(G)^(r)|?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. When do we have (almost) equality in ( 1) ? What conditions on G are sufficient to guarantee (almost) equality ?

accepted.question_text: For the cycle C_n and the path P_n, is the width of the independence complex equal to the size of its largest layer; that is, do we have s(C_n)=max_r |Q(C_n)^(r)| and s(P_n)=max_r |Q(P_n)^(r)|?
accepted.context_brief: Exact Sperner analogues for paths and cycles

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.8. s(Cn) = max r |Q(Cn) (r)| and s(Pn) = max r |Q(Pn) (r)|.

accepted.question_text: Fix p=c/n with c>0. Is it true that, with high probability for G_{n,p}, the width s(G_{n,p}) of the independence complex satisfies s(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1)) max_r |Q(G_{n,p})^(r)|?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9. Let p = cn−1, for some constant c > 0. Is it true with high probability that s(Gn,p) = (1 + o(1)) max r |Q(Gn,p) (r)|?

accepted.question_text: If G_n is an n-vertex 4-chromatic graph such that deleting any edge makes it 3-chromatic, must its minimum degree be o(n) as n→∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 (Paul Erdős, via M. Simonovits). Is it true that if Gn is a 4-chromatic n-vertex graph and deleting any edge of it we get a 3-chromatic graph, then the minimum degree of Gn is o(n) (as n → ∞)?

accepted.question_text: Given an n-vertex planar graph G, can one find in polynomial time an independent set of size floor(n/4)+1, or alternatively prove that obtaining such a set is NP-hard?
accepted.context_brief: Independent sets above the planar n/4 threshold

evidence.quote: Question 5.2. For a given n-vertex planar graph G, is it possible to find in polynomial time (or to show that this is NP-hard) an independent set of size bn/4c + 1?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph containing an edge e that lies in exactly two Hamiltonian cycles?
accepted.context_brief: Hamiltonian cycles through a fixed edge

evidence.quote: Problem 5.3. Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph having an edge e such that there are precisely two Hamiltonian cycles containing e?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph that has exactly four Hamiltonian cycles?
accepted.context_brief: Counting Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite graphs

evidence.quote: Problem 5.4. Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph having precisely 4 Hamiltonian cycles?

accepted.question_text: Is there a family of cubic, cyclically 4-edge-connected Hamiltonian graphs for which Thomason's lollipop method for finding a second Hamiltonian cycle requires superpolynomially many steps?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.5. Does there exist a family of cubic, cyclically 4-edge-connected Hamiltonian graphs for which the lollipop method takes superpolynomially many steps?

accepted.question_text: For the shift graphs defined from cyclically ordered point sets and short vertex sets, determine the exact chromatic numbers of these graphs, especially for vertices given by 2-subsets or 3-subsets under the prescribed intertwining patterns.
accepted.context_brief: Chromatic numbers of cyclic shift graphs

evidence.quote: Problem 5.6. Determine the exact chromatic numbers for these graphs.

accepted.question_text: For every graph G and every integer r≥2, determine or estimate mcr(G,r), the infimum of the maximum average degree mad(F) over graphs F satisfying the vertex-Ramsey property F→(G)^v_r.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.7. Determine or estimate mcr(G, r) for every graph G and r ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: Determine the exact value of mcr(S_2,3), where S_2 is the 2-edge star and mcr(G,r) is the infimum of maximum average degrees of graphs that are vertex-Ramsey for G under r colours.
accepted.context_brief: Three-colour vertex-Ramsey threshold for a 2-edge star

evidence.quote: Problem 5.8. Determine mcr(S2, 3) (no monetary award for that!)

accepted.question_text: If a graph G on n vertices has maximum degree Δ(G)≥n/3, is it true that G has edge-chromatic number χ'(G)=Δ(G) exactly when G contains no overfull subgraph H with e(H)>Δ(G) floor(|H|/2)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.1 (Overfull subgraph conjecture). A graph G on n vertices with ∆(G) ≥ n/3 satisfies χ0(G) = ∆(G) if and only if G contains no overfull subgraph.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a sequence of finite graphs (G_n) such that for every infection probability p>0, majority bootstrap percolation on G_n infects every vertex with probability tending to 1 as n→∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1. Does there exist a sequence of graphs (Gn)n∈N such that for every p > 0: limn→∞ Pp(A(Gn)) = 1 ?

accepted.question_text: Construct an explicit family of invertible n×n matrices over F_2 whose row-reduction distance D(m) from the identity is provably large, specifically either at least 100n or at least n log n, where D(m) is the minimum number of row operations needed to reduce m to the identity.
accepted.context_brief: Hard explicit matrices over F_2 for row reduction

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2. 1. Give an explicit (non-random) example of an matrix m ∈ GL(n, 2) such that D(m) ≥ 100n 2. Give an explicit example of an matrix m ∈ GL(n, 2) such that D(m) ≥ n log n

accepted.question_text: For all integers k≥3 and 1≤ℓ≤k−1, is the minimum number sat(n,k,ℓ) of edges in an ℓ-Hamiltonian-saturated k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices of order Θ(n^ℓ)?

evidence.quote: Together, we proved that for all k ≥ 3 and ` = 1, as well as for all 4/5 k ≤ ` ≤ k − 1 sat(n, k, `) = Θ(n`) , and conjectured that (2) holds for all k and 1 ≤ ` ≤ k−1.

accepted.question_text: Among simple cubic graphs on n vertices, what is the best possible upper bound on the number of cycles of length n/2?

evidence.quote: How many n/2-cycles can a cubic graph have? Given a simple cubic graph with n vertices, what is a good upper bound on the number of cycles of length n/2 it can have?

accepted.question_text: Let a(n) be the maximum size of the automorphism group of a 3-connected cubic graph with n vertices. Is it true that a(n)<n·2^{n/4} for every n≥16?

evidence.quote: Let a(n) be the greatest order of the automorphism group of a 3-connected cubic graph with n vertices. I conjecture: for n ≥ 16, a(n) < n 2 n/4.

accepted.question_text: For fixed n, is P(n,k), the proportion of n×n nonnegative integer matrices with all row and column sums equal to k that have no zero entries, an increasing function of k for every k≥n?
accepted.context_brief: Monotonicity in the Birkhoff polytope lattice-point model

evidence.quote: Obviously P(n, k) = 0 for k < n. It seems obvious that P(n, k) should be increasing as a function of k when n is fixed and k ≥ n, but can you prove it?

accepted.question_text: Given a finite set E and a collection of finite sequences of elements of E that are intended to be simple paths, can one decide efficiently whether there exists a graph whose edge set is E and whose simple paths include exactly those sequences?
accepted.context_brief: Reconstructing a graph from edge-path data

evidence.quote: We now wish to determine if there is a graph such that E is the edges of the graph and the sequences are (nice, simple) paths in the graph. This can be done, the graph would have at most 2|E| vertices so you can search all possibilities. So the question would be whether you can do it efficiently.

accepted.question_text: If a graph G has chromatic number at least r, must its crossing number satisfy cr(G)≥cr(K_r)?

evidence.quote: Albertson’s Conjecture: If χ(G) ≥ r, then the crossing number cr(G) ≥ cr(Kr).

accepted.question_text: For sufficiently large k, does every planar graph G with maximum degree at most 2k+2 admit a (k,k)-colouring, meaning a partition V(G)=J∪K with maximum degrees Δ(G[J])≤k and Δ(G[K])≤k?
accepted.context_brief: Brooks-type improper colouring for planar graphs

evidence.quote: Corréa, Havet, and Sereni [1], conjectured that for sufficiently large k (say, k > 106), every planar graph G with ∆(G) ≤ 2k + 2 has a (k, k)-coloring.

accepted.question_text: Let f(k) be the maximum chromatic number of a circle graph with clique number k. Improve the known bounds on f(k), either by proving a stronger lower bound or a stronger upper bound.
accepted.context_brief: Chromatic number versus clique number in circle graphs

evidence.quote: The lower bound is only barely superlinear, and the upper is very superlinear. It would be interesting to improve any of them.

accepted.question_text: For each r, does there exist a constant m(r) such that the vertex set of any r-mean edge-coloured graph can be partitioned into at most m(r) monochromatic cycles?
accepted.context_brief: Monochromatic cycle partitions in mean colourings

evidence.quote: Question 8.3. Does there exist a constant m(r), depending only on r, such that the vertex set of any r-mean coloured graph may be partitioned into at most m(r) cycles?

accepted.question_text: Let L be an infinite family of forbidden bipartite graphs and let L_m={L∈L:v(L)≤m}. If ex_t(n,L)=O(n^{1+α}) for some α>0, must it follow that for every ε>0 there exists m large enough such that ex_t(n,L_m)=O(n^{1+α+ε}) as n→∞?
accepted.context_brief: Continuity of extremal exponents for infinite families

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1 (Continuity of the exponent). Let L denote an infinite family of bipartite (excluded) graphs and Lm := {L : L ∈ L, v(L) ≤ m}. Is it true that if for some α > 0 and c > 0 we have extt(n,L) = O(n1+α), then for any ε > 0, we have ext(n,Lm) = O(n1+α+ε), as n → ∞, if m is large enough?

accepted.question_text: When k is a field of characteristic different from 2 and G is a 3-edge-connected graph, does the cycle space C(G) admit a natural explicit basis consisting of cycles indexed by the edges of G?
accepted.context_brief: Explicit cycle bases over fields of odd characteristic

evidence.quote: Question: Is there a nice explicit basis for C(G) consisting of cycles indexed by E, assuming G is 3-edge-connected?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a 3-tournament T^3_n whose smallest dominating set has size at least 2014?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.2. There exists a 3-tournament T3 n such that dom(T3 n) ≥ 2014.

accepted.question_text: If every 4-vertex subset of a 3-tournament contains at least two triples with the same root, must the tournament have domination number at most 2014?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.3. If any four vertices of a 3-tournament T3 n contain at least two triples with the same root then dom(Tn) ≤ 2014.

accepted.question_text: For every graph G, is the strong chromatic number sχ(G) always either the biclique number ω_b(G) or exactly one more, i.e. does ω_b(G)≤sχ(G)≤ω_b(G)+1 hold universally?
accepted.context_brief: Strong chromatic number versus biclique number

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.4. ωb(G) ≤ sχ(G) ≤ ωb(G) + 1

accepted.question_text: How many edges must be deleted from an n-vertex K_r-free graph in order to make it bipartite?
accepted.context_brief: Edge deletions to bipartite structure in K_r-free graphs

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. How many edges do we need to delete to make a Kr-free graph G of order n bipartite?

accepted.question_text: For the 3-uniform Ramsey number r(C_3,K_t), where C_3 is the 3-uniform loose triangle, is it true that r(C_3,K_t)=o(t^{3/2})?
accepted.context_brief: Hypergraph Ramsey growth for C3 versus Kt

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.1. (Kostochka-Mubayi-Verstraëte) For k = 3, we have r(C3, Kt) = o(t3/2).

accepted.question_text: What is the computational complexity of finding a longest directed path from x to y in a tournament when x and y are specified vertices?
accepted.context_brief: Longest prescribed-endpoint path in a tournament

evidence.quote: Problem 10.4 (Conjecture 9.1). [3] What is the complexity of finding the longest (x, y)-path in a tournament?

accepted.question_text: What is the computational complexity of the Hamiltonian path problem for path-mergeable digraphs?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.6. [3] What is the complexity of the hamiltonian path problem for path-mergeable digraphs?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an n×n array with entries from {0,...,n} such that each nonzero symbol appears in at most n−2 positions. Must there always exist a Latin square L on symbols {1,...,n} such that L_{i,j}≠A_{i,j} for every cell?
accepted.context_brief: Avoiding sparse forbidden entries in Latin squares

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.7. For any A there exists a latin square L, using the symbols {1, . . . , n} such Li,j 6= Ai,j

accepted.question_text: For every k-arc-strong tournament T, is the minimum number α_k(T) of arcs in a spanning subdigraph with minimum in-degree and out-degree at least k always equal to the minimum number β_k(T) of arcs in a spanning k-arc-strong subdigraph? In particular, is β_k(T)≤nk+k(k−1)/2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.3. [2] For every k arc-stroing tournament T we have αk(T) = βk(T), in particular we have βk(T) ≤ nk + k(k−1)/2.

accepted.question_text: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a k-arc-strong tournament T=(V,A), finds a minimum-size arc set A0 of size β_k(T) whose induced spanning subdigraph is already k-arc-strong?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithms for minimum k-arc-strong spanning subdigraphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.4. [2] There exists a polynomial algorithm for finding, in a given k-arc-strong tournament T = (V, A) a minimum set of arcs A0 (of size βk(T)) such that the subdigraph induced by A0 is already k-arc-strong.

accepted.question_text: If a family F of subsets of [n] is an antichain and has diameter at most n−k, meaning |A△B|≤n−k for every A,B in F, must the Milner bound |F|≤binom(n, ceil((n+k)/2)) still hold?

evidence.quote: Question. Does the bound (4) still hold for antichains satisfying the weaker condition that the diameter of F is at most n − k?

accepted.question_text: Given positive integers k and r, does there exist n such that every k-colouring of the symmetric group S_n contains a monochromatic copy of S_r, where a copy of S_r means the set of all r! concatenations of some partition of the symbols into r disjoint words?

evidence.quote: Question 12.1. Given k and r, does there exist n such that whenever the symmetric group Sn is k-coloured there is a monochromatic copy of Sr?

trace.notes: Resolved the arXiv abs URL to the PDF, read the full 29-page source, identified it as a curated open-problem collection, and mapped problem-bearing sections 2 through 12.
Extracted explicit conjectures, questions, and problem statements from seminar and early problem-session sections, including items 2.1-2.14, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.9, 5.1-5.8, 6.1, and 7.1-7.3.
Extracted explicit and clearly stated open questions and conjectures from later problem sessions, including sections 8.1-12.1.
Rewrote each candidate into a standalone question by inlining local definitions when they were necessary to understand the statement without referring back to the source.
No near-duplicate question clusters required merging; distinct problem statements were preserved separately.

Accepted only items with direct verbatim support visible in the source and enough local context to make the rewrite self-contained; all accepted items are marked unsolved because the source does not explicitly mark them as solved.
